topic.title: The exit email where everyone is in cc
topic.claim: The last leverage an Indian employee has on the way out is embarrassment, which is why a resignation can end with the CEO, HR and the whole team on one email.
topic.behaviour: Serving notice, getting a few exit documents and a salary on day 9, then facing silence on calls and mails for the rest, and finally sending a warning mail to the founder with HR and the team copied so the company has to reply.
topic.mechanism: Once you leave, the company has no reason to answer you and you have no formal power. Visibility is the only force left, so cc becomes a weapon. It's also why people stay quiet and polite in notice periods: nobody wants to burn the last bridge before the paperwork is done.
real_details: The poster left after serving notice period
Some exit documents arrived within a few days and salary on the 9th day
After that the company ignored calls and mails about the remaining documents and clarifications
The poster sent a warning email to the CEO/founder with HR and the whole team in cc
The poster says they made sure the company had enough reasons to reply
topic.why_now: It's appraisal and job-switch season, and a multi-part thread on this is getting traction.

sources.fact: Under Section 17(2) of the Code on Wages, 2019, employers must complete full and final settlement within two working days of an employee's exit, including resignation.
sources.excerpt: employers "must complete full and final settlement within two working days of an employee's exit." ... "introduced under Section 17(2) of the Code on Wages, 2019, seeks to end this practice." ... all dues must be cleared "within two working days of resignation, termination, retrenchment, or closure." ... the Labour Codes are "formally notified and now in the implementation phase."

sources.fact: When an employer goes silent on F&F, the formal routes are a legal notice or a Labour Commissioner complaint, and withholding a relieving letter to deny F&F is called unethical and challengeable.
sources.excerpt: a delay becomes legally unreasonable when it "crosses 45 days without valid justification." ... "Demand payment within 7–15 days." ... "Legal notices often prompt employers to comply." ... Labour Commissioner complaint is "cost-effective and fast." ... Relieving letters are not mandatory under law, but holding one back to deny F&F payment "is unethical and may be challenged." ... "F&F cannot be withheld entirely because of asset disputes."

paragraphs: The day you resign, you lose your power. The only thing left is cc.
We stayed so polite through notice. Every reply soft and quick, because nobody wants to annoy you before the papers come.
A few documents came. Salary on day 9. Then silence.
Once we leave, you have no reason to answer, and we have no formal power. Being seen is all that's left.
So the mail goes to the founder. You in cc. The whole team in cc.
The law says full and final within two working days of exit. Still, we needed an audience.
Honestly, the cc is the only exit process I trust.

draft.caption: What did it finally take for your old company to reply about your exit documents?
draft.alt_text: A single text slide. It opens by saying that the day you resign, you lose your power, and the only thing left is cc. Then it becomes an open letter to HR. It says employees stay polite through the notice period so they don't annoy HR before the papers come. A few documents arrive, salary comes on day 9, and then there is silence. It explains that once someone leaves, the company has no reason to answer and the employee has no formal power, so being seen is all that's left. That is why the mail goes to the founder with HR and the whole team in cc. It notes that the law requires full and final settlement within two working days of exit, yet people still need an audience. It ends with the writer saying the cc is the only exit process she trusts.
